kernel: the decode and prefill attention family around the stock path: dec_attn split-K (MiMo 192/128 global layers), the packed-KV quantized-cache decode (msv_qkv_mpp matmul2d tile and the plain qkvDecKernel), the fused QK-norm+RoPE kernels (hd 128 and hd 256), the msv_attn_p256 head-dim-256 prefill flash kernel, MLX's sdpa_vector grouping split, and the sliding-window trim
summary: Decode and verify attention: dec_attn.zig serves MiMo's global layers (q/k 192, v 128) with a KV group's query heads times query positions (1 at decode, up to 8 in a verify) as the rows of one MMA tile, split-K over 32-key tiles, engaging at one row only from 8192 keys and held to a 2x-of-stock error bar. Quantized caches read through two packed kernels tried before dense: the matmul2d tensor-op tile (msv_qkv_mpp, 32-token KV pages dequantized into threadgroup tile memory, one thread per padded softmax row, split-KV partials merged) inside the qkvMppWins window, and a plain block kernel capped near 10 KiB of threadgroup memory. msv_attn_p256 is the head-dim-256 prefill flash kernel (64-row query tile, 32-key blocks, 8 simdgroups, exp2 softmax, fp32 carry across budgeted key-axis dispatches) that declines under 16 query rows; widths 2..15 at hd 256 split into groups of min(8, 32/gqa) for MLX's sdpa_vector instead, and sliding-window layers trim every read to the window. A fused QK-norm+RoPE kernel pair (hd 128 decode, hd 256 for 1..32 rows) serves the projection chain with cos/sin rows probed out of stock mlx_fast_rope.

notes: Doc-vs-source checks, sided with the source. (1) Our doc's 'structure after Inco Splash' phrase for the packed-KV kernel has no counterpart in the clone; the kernel's design comments instead cite docs/kv-quant-perf.md (src/transformer.zig:16160, 16207, 17247), which is ABSENT from the tree at this rev, so the Phase 0/1/2 tables behind the fused-quant gate could not be read. (2) Our doc says MLX's fused kernel 'refuses q_len * gqa > 32, so causal verify widths 2 to 15 are split'; the source predicate is the negation of (q_len <= 8 and q_len * gqa <= 32) at hd {64, 96, 128, 256} (src/transformer.zig:8302-8306), so a width 9..15 block splits even when q_len * gqa <= 32, because q_len > 8 leaves MLX's vector kernel at hd 256, and the split default is measured at hd 256 only (Flash-Next gqa 12). (3) Two different floors sit under 'packed-KV eligibility': the fused-route per-layer floor KV_ATTN_FUSED_MIN_TK = 2048 for t_q 1 (src/transformer.zig:17267) versus the matmul2d tile window qkvMppWins (2048 at t_q >= 4, 8192 at 2..3, 16384 at 1, src/transformer.zig:17096-17099). Our doc's 'tried first and declines outside a window' is the tile window; below it the plain decode kernel still serves t_q 1 from the 2048 floor, and upstream's own perf table says packed reads are 'auto from 8K' (docs/performance.md:61), which matches neither constant. (4) Our doc's '1.7x slower' for the large-threadgroup form: the source's measured A/B is 1.9 vs 1.1 ms with 24 KiB score buffers, while the 28 KiB figure is the footprint statement on the same comment; both live at src/transformer.zig:16192-16195. (5) The verify-width eligibility bug our doc attributes to the packed-KV path: the source locates it at kvAttnFusedEligible admitting T_q 2..32 that fell to the composed qmm chain (src/transformer.zig:47470-47479), the same gate our item 4 covers. Other caveats. The dec_attn reference sentence does not restate its machine; the MiMo section's measurements are M5 Ultra, and the 48 -> 18 misroute comment names the 27B but no machine, while the 28-vs-60 A/B names M4 Max. Both custom decode paths are explicitly not bit-identical: dec_attn holds a 2x-of-stock test bar (src/dec_attn.zig:318) and the packed decode is pinned no-worse-than-reference with a different reduction order (src/transformer.zig:16178-16180). kv_mpp_bits accepts 4 and 8 with at most 8 dequant groups per row; the doc's '32-token KV pages' is QKV_MPP_PAGE and the kernel's N = 32. The qk-norm+RoPE fusion our doc describes at head dim 256 serving 1 to 32 rows is fusedQkNormRope256; a separate hd-128 decode variant (one threadgroup per head) serves the same lever at 128. msv_attn_p256's causal arm also yields to MLX's NAX fused kernel where that is preferred (fusedSdpa256Prefill, src/transformer.zig:3477-3481), and the sink arm (fusedSinkAttnPrefill) serves MiMo's 192/128 with no kill switch because no composed score tensor is billed there. The sliding trim numbers are decode; the same table's Laguna XS rows (prompt and decode) are in the clone but belong to a different model family. Every measured number here is upstream's own under its conditions; none was re-measured.
